sentences.text: For a Tier 3 UCB, the no-charge rule for business-purpose loans to individuals and MSEs applies only up to a sanctioned amount/limit of ₹50 lakh, and this loan is ₹80 lakh, so that specific prohibition does not apply here. [E2, E6]

For cases other than those covered by that no-charge rule, pre-payment charges, if any, are to be as per the approved policy of the UCB, and for term loans they are to be based on the amount being prepaid. [E8, E9]

The directions also require the applicability of pre-payment charges to be clearly disclosed in the sanction letter and loan agreement, and they bar any pre-payment charge that has not been disclosed as specified. [E12, E14]

So, the 2% pre-payment charge mentioned in the sanction letter is not itself shown by the cited directions to be a violation for this Tier 3 UCB, but whether it is allowed still depends on the bank’s approved policy and the disclosure requirement. [E8, E9, E12, E14]
